# Libraries

```{r message=FALSE}
library(HDF5Array)
library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(cellhashR)
library(DropletUtils)
library(scater)
library(scuttle)
library(scales)
library(ggExtra)
```


```{r}
set.seed(12)
```

# Data Loading & SCE object creation

To load the information contained on a h5 file, use `read10xCounts` because it handles automatically the loading of both mRNA data and ATAC data. `read10xCounts` returns a SCE object with all the information. Make sure to split the data so the object contains two separated experiments, one for gene expression and the other for epigenetics, `peaks`.


```{r}
# Loading data
sce <- read10xCounts("data/muA/filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5")
# spitting by type, i.e. mRNA & ATAC sequencing
sce <- splitAltExps(sce, rowData(sce)[, "Type"])
# remember to swap experiments to work with the count matrix of your experiment
sce <- swapAltExp(sce, "Gene Expression")

# set row names as unique to avoid redundancy
rownames(sce) <- make.unique(rowData(sce)$Symbol)
# set colnames as the cell barcode
colnames(sce) <- colData(sce)$"Barcode"
```


```{r}
sce
```


```{r}
# using DropletUtils::read10xCounts
htos <- read10xCounts("data/muA/muAh/raw_feature_bc_matrix.h5")
colnames(htos) <- htos$Barcode
htos <- htos[, intersect(colnames(sce), colnames(htos))]
```

```{r}
# make sure that the colnames are the same in both assays
stopifnot(setequal(colnames(htos), colnames(sce)))
```

Lastly, add the hto data as an alternative experiment.

```{r}
altExp(sce, "hto") <- SummarizedExperiment(assay(htos))

# hto can be removed

#rm(htos)
```


# Demultiplexing

Set a list containing the HTO tags of interest. It will be used to filter out those non interesting tags.

```{r}
HTO_tag=c("HTO-1","HTO-2","HTO-3","HTO-4","HTO-5","HTO-6","HTO-7","HTO-8","HTO-9","HTO-10")
```


# All-in-One

```{r}
source("lib_QC.R")
```

Another option is to call the holistic function `QC` which will handle everything for you. Just make sure to pass the appropriate parameters:

- sce_objec is a SingleCellExperiment object containing your count matrix as main experiment.

- organism, either "mouse" or "human", to target mitochondrial genes accordingly.

- hto, either `TRUE` or `FALSE` according to whether you have HTO tags on your experiment.

- methods, list of methods which can be passed to `GenerateCellHashingCalls()` to carry out demultiplexing.

- project, character string indicating the subfolder where to store graphical outputs. As default it is set to "New_folder", generating the path `pdf/1-Loading/New_project`.

- HTO_tag is a list containing the HTO tags one wants to keep.

- filter_singlet, either `TRUE` or `FALSE` to whether keep solely cell barcodes identified as singlet or not.

- mito_max, numeric value indicating the maximum cutoff for percentage of mitochondrial genes.

- min_nfeatures, numeric value indicating the minimum cutoff for number of features in log10 scale.

- normalization_method, method to choose as normalization strategy. The options are `logNorm`, `SCTransform` and `AnPearson`.

- workers, set the number of CPU cores you would like to use. *Helpful for UMAP computation*.




```{r warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=FALSE} 
sce_2 <- QC(sce_object = sce,
            organism = "mouse",
            hto=TRUE,
            methods=c("multiseq","gmm_demux", "htodemux", "dropletutils"),
            project="test",
            HTO_tag=HTO_tag,
            filter_singlet=FALSE,
            mito_max=15,
            min_nfeatures=200,
            normalization_method="logNorm",
            seed=12,
            workers = 16)
```



# Demo with GEO dataset GSE190012
https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE213828 

```{r}
count_m <- read.delim("../notebooks/querying/geo_data/GSE213828/GSE213828_merged_counts.txt.gz")
metaD <- read.delim("../notebooks/querying/geo_data/GSE213828/GSE213828_merged_sample_info.txt.gz",row.names = "qp_well_fq")

demo_geo <- SingleCellExperiment(list(counts=data.matrix(count_m[,-1:-2])),
                     rowData=count_m[,1:2],
                     colData=metaD,mainExpName = "Gene Expression")
rownames(demo_geo) <- make.unique(mcols(demo_geo)$gene_name)
```




```{r}
demo_geo
```



```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
demo_geo <- QC(sce_object = demo_geo,
            organism = "mouse",
            hto=FALSE,
            methods=c("multiseq","gmm_demux", "htodemux", "dropletutils"),
            project="demo_GSE213828",
            HTO_tag=HTO_tag,
            filter_singlet=FALSE,
            mito_max=15,
            min_nfeatures=3000,
            normalization_method="logNorm",
            seed=12,
            workers = 16)
```
